unverified.why: SafepointEnd is OFF in all three JFCs. SafepointBegin is committed after synchronize + cleanup, before the VM operation runs (verified in jdk21u safepoint.cpp), so its duration is not the full pause. Catalogue uses SafepointBegin.duration + ExecuteVMOperation.duration joined on safepointId; ExecuteVMOperation has threshold 0/1/10 ms, so on medium/low short operations are missing and the end phase is never counted. Not yet checked on a real recording.

Which field async-profiler 4.5 sets as the sample weight in its ObjectAllocationInNewTLAB/OutsideTLAB events (allocationSize vs tlabSize) is not confirmed; the sample file has 24 InNewTLAB and 0 OutsideTLAB events.
Horvitz–Thompson correction for the AP shared-bucket lock sampler is a draft formula (collection doc, "Verify on kind"). The sample recording has 0 JavaMonitorEnter/ThreadPark events.

JavaErrorThrow is emitted from the Error constructor. HotSpot can throw preallocated OutOfMemoryError objects for heap exhaustion, which may not emit JavaErrorThrow. Heap OOM detection from JavaErrorThrow alone is not verified; MetaspaceOOM is a dedicated event.

Whether jdk.MethodTiming invocations/average/maximum are cumulative since instrumentation or per emission period is not verified on JDK 25. Δinvocations assumes cumulative; if per-period, avg/max per window are direct.

Locked name says "process"; the data is the container cgroup (ContainerCPUUsage). CPULoad.jvmUser+jvmSystem is per-process but its normalisation inside a CPU-limited container was not verified, so it is not used for the ratio.
carrierThread, pinnedReason and blockingOperation exist on JDK 25 only (21 has duration + stack only), verified from jfr metadata. by=carrier|reason returns not_on_this_jdk on 21.
jdk.TLSHandshake has a duration field on 17/21 but not on 25 (jfr metadata). No duration is exposed in the catalogue.
JFC sets no threshold for TLSHandshake; recorded behaviour assumes the event default (all handshakes). Not checked on a recording.
Both events do not exist in JDK 25 metadata. ZUnmap is used by zgc-alloc (17/21 only); GCLocker is enabled but not mapped to any metric.

unverified.item: Enabled events not mapped to a metric
unverified.why: G1BasicIHOP, G1AdaptiveIHOP, GCLocker, EvacuationFailed, PromotionFailed, SystemGC, HeapDump, ProcessStart, RedefineClasses, RetransformClasses, ReservedStackActivation, NativeLibraryLoad/Unload, PhysicalMemory, SwapSpace, flag-change, configuration and recording-health events. They feed incident evidence, INFO chips, get_jvm_info or Recording health, not query_metric series; no locked chart covers IHOP.
GCHeapMemoryUsage does not exist on 17 (verified); the 17 fallback is per-GC GCHeapSummary points, so the heap trend on 17 has one point per GC, not one per second.
MetaspaceSummary is GC-linked (before/after each GC), so the overview key and trend have one point per GC; a JVM with few GCs may return not_enough_data.

Carried over from get_jvm_info: whether flags from JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS (MaxMetaspaceSize, MaxDirectMemorySize) appear in jvmArguments is not verified, so limit=MaxMetaspaceSize / MaxDirectMemorySize may read "not set" wrongly.
Fields checked in jfr metadata for JDK 21 and 25 on the box; JDK 17 relies on the earlier metadata dump. Which collectors emit PromotionFailed not checked on a real recording.
